acceptance.criterion_verbatim: O4-AC1 -- the federated answer carries a VINTAGE line naming each catalog joined and its build time.
acceptance.output_evidence: rc=0. The deciding line: 'VINTAGE: 2 catalog(s) joined (code_heat, iceberg), 2 table(s), 1 measured / 1 UNREAD -- the ARTIFACT's build time, never the query's clock'. Then, one line per table with its own claim: '  code_heat.globgrph.code_heat  build_time=2026-07-16T03:40:46Z  claim=measured  age=51.1d' followed by '      instrument: max(s3 LastModified) over 2 of 2 object(s) under s3://opal-313476888478-globgrph/warehouse/code_heat/; located by glue:GetTable globgrph.code_heat -> s3://opal-313476888478-globgrph/warehouse/code_heat/'; and '  iceberg.globgrph.graph_nodes  build_time=UNREAD  claim=absent' followed by '      reason: listing did not complete within this table's probe ceiling (9001 object(s) read under s3://opal-313476888478-globgrph/warehouse/globgrph/graph_nodes_4c6c23bd-fffa-427e-9cd9-7a9deaa3426d/); S3 lists lexicographically, not by time, so no max is claimed from a partial read'. The block closes with '  the query clock (2026-09-05T05:46:12Z) is NOT a vintage and is printed here only so the two cannot be confused'. NOTE ON THE PATH THIS INVOCATION TAKES, stated because it is load-bearing rather than incidental: --budget 120 is BELOW comp-heat's own FEDERATED_LIVE_FLOOR_S (200 s), so the tool prints 'comp-heat federated: refusing to dispatch to the LIVE Trino plane' and NO Trino query is dispatched. The vintage block is printed on that path deliberately -- an artifact's build time is a property of the artifact, not of whether this process queried it, and the refuse path is the only one any sub-floor caller can reach. BEFORE this change, at b630052d6a, the same invocation printed the budget line and the refusal and nothing about what it would have read.
acceptance.denominator: 2 of 2 catalogs joined are NAMED (derived from the SQL about to run, not from a constant); 1 of 2 tables reports a measured build time, 1 of 2 reports UNREAD with its reason. 3 of 3 consecutive runs returned rc=0 with an identical VINTAGE header and an identical code_heat build_time; the only run-to-run variation is the iceberg row's own bounded-probe progress (scanned 9001 / 9001 / 10001), which is printed rather than smoothed.
acceptance.status_reason: Graded on the printed block, which carries the catalog list, a per-table build time or a per-table reason, and the instrument that produced each. The values that decide it are a COUNT (2 catalogs, 1 measured, 1 UNREAD) and a FIXED TIMESTAMP (2026-07-16T03:40:46Z, stable across 6 readings this session), not a duration -- so the pass does not rest on a wall-clock reading. A live-plane read is not reproducible the way a git count is; the vintage of every reading here is 2026-09-05 ~05:0x-05:5xZ and is stated rather than implied.

THE VALUE DOES EXIST once the listing completes: max(LastModified) = 2026-09-05T02:11:10Z, about three hours before this read. CONSEQUENCE, recorded not judged: the two sides of the federated join differ in age by roughly 51 days -- the graph side hours old, the code_heat side frozen since 2026-07-16T03:40:46Z. The code_heat freeze is 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~W's measurement on OS-s-7 (producer host-bound by a CTO revert 2026-07-16, 0 of 142 EventBridge rules fire it, Glue Owner null) and is CITED, not re-derived; this worker's tool independently re-reads the same object plane and prints the same timestamp, which is corroboration on the CLIENT axis (boto3 vs the .tools/aws CLI) and NOT independent on the PLANE axis -- stated so agreement is not mistaken for two instruments. The join was never run -- comp-heat refuses to dispatch below 200 s and this order's invocation is 120 s -- so what a 51-day skew does to a consumer's question belongs to OS-s-8 and OS-s-10, not to this cell.
